claims.text_en: Thon Buri is one of Bangkok's 50 khets, 8.551 km2 on the west bank, with seven khwaeng: Wat Kanlaya (0.785 km2, 7,739 people), Hiran Ruchi (0.691, 10,788), Bang Yi Ruea (1.523, 18,470), Bukkhalo (1.210, 16,075), Talat Phlu (1.823, 15,221), Dao Khanong (1.289, 16,581) and Samre (1.230, 13,412) - 98,286 registered residents in Dec 2023. Boundaries (Thai Wikipedia): north - Bangkok Yai and Phra Nakhon along Khlong Bangkok Yai and the river midline; east - Khlong San via the Memorial Bridge, Prajadhipok, Lat Ya and Somdet Chao Phraya roads and Khlong Bang Sai Kai; south - Bang Kho Laem and Rat Burana along the river and Khlong Dao Khanong; west - Chom Thong and Phasi Charoen along Khlong Bang Sakae and allies. History: the area was King Taksin's capital 1767-1782; the amphoe was Ratchakhrue, renamed Bang Yi Ruea (11 Jul 1916) then Thon Buri (17 Apr 1939), becoming a khet in 1972; khwaeng Samre and Dao Khanong were created 1 Dec 2003.

question_answers.question: identity/scope
question_answers.answer: Khet Thon Buri, 8.551 km2, seven khwaeng (Wat Kanlaya, Hiran Ruchi, Bang Yi Ruea, Bukkhalo, Talat Phlu, Dao Khanong, Samre), bounded by Khlong Bangkok Yai + river (N), Khlong Bang Sai Kai/Taksin/Prajadhipok roads (E vs Khlong San), river + Khlong Dao Khanong (S), khlongs (W vs Chom Thong/Phasi Charoen). In-polygon anchors: Talat Phlu market, Wat Kalayanamit, Bukkhalo, the Wongwian Yai circle, SRT Wongwian Yai, BTS Pho Nimit/Talat Phlu/Wutthakat. Out: BTS Wongwian Yai (Khlong San khet), Santa Cruz/Kudi Chin north tip (polygon clip), Siriraj (Bangkok Noi), BRT Ratchaphruek terminus (Rat Burana side).

question_answers.question: everyday experience
question_answers.answer: A low-rise family khet of markets, temples and schools strung along the BTS Silom band: Talat Phlu's century market street, Bukkhalo and Samre neighbourhoods, Wongwian Yai's bus-rail junction; the riverfront Wat Kanlaya strip is the heritage exception. Population down 57% since 1992 leaves older stock and thinning footfall; subarea claims marked partial.

question_answers.question: values+mechanisms
question_answers.answer: Transport 8 = three in-polygon BTS stations + SRT Wongwian Yai terminal + major bus hub + 12 main roads/4 bridges (BTS Wongwian Yai itself across the boundary). Rent 9 = cheapest portal pricing of the batch (1-bed avg USD 387, page-one from 11,500 THB) on falling demand. Food 8 = Talat Phlu's decades-old shop layer plus neighbourhood markets. Vibe 8 = old-community texture the film spotlight amplified.

question_answers.question: counter-evidence
question_answers.answer: Green 4 is confirmed as honestly low - no district-scale park exists in the khet (two OSM passes + both wikis agree; the main named green is a ~10-rai pocket park). No hospital is verified inside the khet (Siriraj is Bangkok Noi; Somdech Phra Pinklao excluded by polygon). The brief's 'between the river and the expressway' framing does not hold - the expressway runs through neighbouring khets.

question_answers.question: rhythm
question_answers.answer: Market mornings at Talat Phlu; school and commute pulses along the BTS band and Wongwian Yai junction; the Maeklong train passes through the market street on schedule; evenings are local and early - the khet has no late-night anchor of its own.

question_answers.question: walkability
question_answers.answer: Flat canal-grid streets; the Talat Phlu market-to-BTS relationship (~1 km walk per TAT) and the rail-adjacent shop lines make the central khwaeng walkable at block scale; Intharaphitak/Isaraphap traffic is the hostile axis; no walking durations were derived from catchment radius in this bundle.

question_answers.question: daily life
question_answers.answer: Everyday needs: Talat Phlu, Samre and Wat Sutharam markets (OSM-mapped) plus the BTS-band malls; schools incl. Rajabhat universities and Suksanaree; healthcare via BMA clinics with full-service hospitals across the boundaries (Taksin Hospital E, Siriraj N). Leisure: temple grounds, the riverside walkway, neighbourhood gyms.

question_answers.question: affordability vs stated figures
question_answers.answer: App 12,000/24,000 matches HipFlat's portal data closely (studio USD 355 ~ 12-13k, 1-bed USD 387 ~ 13-14k, 2-bed USD 652 ~ 22-23k; Talat Phlu cluster 14,500-21,000) - the cheapest of the four batch khets, with prices still falling (-7.0% vs Jan 2026). Rent 9 is defensible.

question_answers.question: green/quiet with polygon honesty
question_answers.answer: Green: app 4.6 ha (0.6%) - the batch's lowest - is consistent with the map (pocket park ~10 rai + sports fields; no district park). Quiet: the interior khwaeng are genuinely quiet in a shrinking-population way; the riverside walkway (05:00-22:00) is the main new public space, and it is a walkway, not a park.

question_answers.question: conditional fit
question_answers.answer: Strong fit: families and long-stayers who want the cheapest rents in the researched core with BTS access, old-market food and heritage riverfronts on weekends. Weak fit: park users (0.6% share), late-night dwellers, and anyone needing a full-service hospital inside the khet.

question_answers.question: recent changes 2024-2026
question_answers.answer: MRT Purple Line southern extension construction through the khet (Wongwian Yai underground interchange; ~2030 target reported); Talat Phlu's 2024 film-fame bump to its food-street profile; the 2021-2023 riverside walkway from the Memorial Bridge to Wat Kalayanamit now in daily public use; portal rents declining through 2026.

question_answers.question: uncertainties/outside-the-score
question_answers.answer: Unresolved: the app's 4.6-ha park composition (pocket-park aggregation presumed); Somdech Phra Pinklao Hospital's khet membership (wikis list it, polygon excludes it); Purple Line opening date (reported ~2030, snippet-level); the Maeklong line's service frequency; the Kudi Chin walkway's formal opening date (walkable since 2023 per aggregated reports). BTS Wongwian Yai's khet membership is RESOLVED: Khlong San, per station infobox + both wikis + PIP.

preview.text_en: Old Thonburi living at the old prices: a century-old market street at Talat Phlu, three BTS stations, King Taksin's riverfront heritage - and almost no public park anywhere in the khet.

guide_lead.text_en: Thon Buri khet is west-bank family Bangkok at its most affordable: seven khwaeng of markets, temples and low-rise streets between the Chao Phraya and the khlongs, served by BTS Pho Nimit, Talat Phlu and Wutthakat plus the Maeklong-line terminal at Wongwian Yai. Registered population has fallen 57% since 1992 to 98,286, rents run from about 11,500 THB, and the food story is Talat Phlu's decades-old shops - nationally famous again after the 2024 film. The trade-offs are structural: the batch's lowest green (4.6 ha, 0.6%), no full-service hospital inside the khet, and the BTS Wongwian Yai terminus itself sitting across the Khlong San line.

strengths.text: Cheapest of the batch with real transit: 1-bed portal averages ~USD 387 (13-14k THB), three in-polygon BTS Silom stations, the Maeklong terminal and the west bank's biggest bus hub.
Authentic old-Bangkok texture: Talat Phlu's 80-year dessert shop and 60-year khao mu dang, the Kudi Chin riverfront and the new Memorial Bridge-to-Wat Kalayanamit walkway.

tradeoffs.text: Green 4 is the honest floor: no district-scale park inside the khet - the main named green is a ~10-rai pocket park, and the riverside showpiece (Chao Phraya Sky Park) is outside the polygon.
No full-service hospital verified inside the khet: Siriraj is Bangkok Noi across the canal, and the wikis' Somdech Phra Pinklao entry falls outside the app polygon too.

day_night.text: Days follow the market-and-school rhythm around Talat Phlu and the BTS band, with the Maeklong train cutting through the market street; nights are local and early - the Wongwian Yai junction quiets with the buses, and the khet has no late-night strip of its own.

within_area_variation.text: The riverfront Wat Kanlaya heritage strip, the Talat Phlu-Bukkhalo market band along the BTS line, and the interior Samre/Wutthakat/Dao Khanong khwaeng are three different neighbourhoods - with the northern tip (Santa Cruz/Kudi Chin) clipped out of the app polygon entirely.

conditional_fit.text: Choose it if cheap long-term rent (12-14k for a 1-bed) with BTS access and an old-market, family-neighbourhood texture outweighs park access and late-night options.
Skip it if you need parks at the door, a hospital in-district, or the named 'Wongwian Yai' BTS address - that terminus is administratively Khlong San's.

uncertainties.text: Unresolved: composition of the app's 4.6-ha park figure; Somdech Phra Pinklao Hospital's true khet membership; Purple Line opening target (~2030, snippet-level); Maeklong-line frequency; Kudi Chin walkway's formal opening date. BTS Wongwian Yai = Khlong San khet is resolved; anchors verified against OSM with no mismatch beyond the northern-tip clip.

open_issues: BTS Wongwian Yai membership resolved (Khlong San khet per station infobox + both wikis' district transport lists + PIP), but the brief expected it in-khet - editorial copy should use SRT Wongwian Yai (Maeklong terminal, in-khet) for the khet's own rail story.
App polygon clips khwaeng Wat Kanlaya's northern tip: Santa Cruz church, Wat Intharam and the Kudi Chin walkway are PIP-OUT despite confirmed in-khet status - coordinator polygon audit recommended.
park_ha 4.6 composition unknown; OSM named green is pocket-scale only - the low green score is honest but the specific 4.6 number is unreproducible.
Somdech Phra Pinklao Hospital: listed by both wikis under the district, PIP-OUT of the polygon (likely Bangkok Noi side) - unresolved.
Purple Line south (through-khet) facts rest on MRTA/search-aggregated reporting, not body-read pages; dates are reported targets.
Population-decline claim rests on Thai Wikipedia's 1992 figure (231,271); no registry source body-read.
